items.prompt: Two leads reassign the same ticket at the same moment. What does the service-layer design (load, then open the transaction, then update by id) produce?
items.answer: Both succeed, the last write wins, and both rows record a stale fromAssigneeId
distractors: The second fails with a serialization error that the client must retry
The second blocks on the row lock that the first transaction took during its read
Only one commits, and the other rolls back with a single history row
items.explanation: requireWorkflowTicket reads with the global client before prisma.$transaction opens, and updateTicket filters by id alone (F8): centralized rules, but not race-safe.

items.prompt: A request to POST /api/tickets/[ticketId]/notes carries a support-hub-session cookie whose value is not valid JSON. What comes back?
items.answer: 401, since an unparsable cookie reads as no session at all
distractors: 500, since JSON.parse throws and nothing catches the error
403, as the cookie exists but carries no role that may write
400 BAD_REQUEST, since the route treats it as a bad request body
items.explanation: readSession wraps JSON.parse in try/catch and returns null on failure. requireSession (via requireRouteSession) then throws unauthorized(), a 401 AppError.

items.prompt: A customer replies to a RESOLVED ticket. What status does it end in, and does the transition table approve?
items.answer: WAITING_ON_CUSTOMER, an edge that the transition table rejects
distractors: OPEN, via the normal reopen edge in the transition table
RESOLVED, since customer replies never change a ticket's status
No status, as the reply is refused with 409 on a RESOLVED ticket
items.explanation: addPublicReply sets WAITING_ON_CUSTOMER for every CUSTOMER_PORTAL author without calling assertValidStatusTransition (F3); the semantics are inverted too, since support is now the one waiting.

items.prompt: A 13:00 first-response deadline is paused from 12:20 and resumed at 14:00. What state is reported at 14:00?
items.answer: BREACHED, because the pause is only a label and no time is credited
distractors: HEALTHY, because the 100 paused minutes push the deadline to 14:40
PAUSED, because the clock stays paused until the next customer reply
AT_RISK, because the moved deadline is inside the at-risk window
items.explanation: evaluateSlaTracking copies accumulatedPauseMs unchanged and resets pausedAt to null on resume; nothing credits the paused time or moves the due date (F4, check C3).

items.prompt: A first response arrives five hours after its deadline. What SLA state is recorded?
items.answer: MET, because actualAt short-circuits before dueAt is compared
distractors: BREACHED, because actualAt is later than dueAt when it is checked
AT_RISK, until a manager acknowledges the late response
PAUSED, because the late response stops the clock for review
items.explanation: Order of checks matters: the actualAt branch short-circuits, so late responses vanish from every BREACHED counter (F5).

items.prompt: With a 15-minute at-risk threshold, what does getSlaState return exactly at the deadline, and 15m59s before it?
items.answer: AT_RISK both times, as neither moment is past the deadline yet
distractors: BREACHED at the due instant, then HEALTHY with 15m59s still to spare
BREACHED once the deadline arrives, while 15m59s out reads AT_RISK
AT_RISK right at the deadline, but HEALTHY when 15m59s remain
items.explanation: isAfter is strict, so exactly at the deadline the ticket is not yet breached; differenceInMinutes truncates 15m59s to 15, which is within the 15-minute threshold (check C6).

items.prompt: A SUPPORT_AGENT adds an internal note to a ticket whose status is CLOSED. What does addInternalNote do?
items.answer: 409: closed tickets must be reopened before internal work continues
distractors: Adds the note, since internal notes are never shown to customers
403: only leads and managers may write on closed tickets
Adds the note and moves the ticket back to OPEN automatically
items.explanation: assertCanAddInternalNote passes for an agent; then if (ticket.status === "CLOSED") throws conflict("Closed tickets must be reopened before internal work continues.") before the transaction.

items.prompt: A READ_ONLY_OBSERVER posts an internal note on an OPEN ticket. What comes back?
items.answer: 403 with "Only internal support staff can add internal notes."
distractors: 200, since observers count as internal users for internal notes
409, since the role check for notes reports a conflict as well
404, since observers cannot load tickets for writing at all
items.explanation: assertCanAddInternalNote requires canModifyTickets, which lists agents, leads and managers only. It throws forbidden(...), a 403, even though isInternalUser includes the observer.

items.prompt: POST /api/tickets with the body `{` versus the body `{}`. Which status codes come back?
items.answer: 500 for `{`, a SyntaxError, and 400 for `{}`, a ZodError from parseJson
distractors: 400 for both, since parseJson validates the raw body and shape
500 for both, as the route wraps neither body in error handling of its own
400 for `{` and 201 for `{}`, since every create field has a default
items.explanation: request.json() throws a SyntaxError before Zod runs and falls through to 500; only a ZodError maps to 400 VALIDATION_ERROR.

items.prompt: A portal user's session email differs from the requester email only in letter case. What do they see?
items.answer: The detail page opens, but the ticket is missing from their list
distractors: They see the ticket both in the list and on its detail page
They see it nowhere, neither in the ticket list nor on the detail page
They see it in the list but get a 403 when opening the detail
items.explanation: Two ownership checks that disagree on normalization produce inconsistent isolation.

items.prompt: A SUPPORT_AGENT asks changeTicketStatus to move a CLOSED ticket to PENDING. Which message comes back with the 409?
items.answer: "Tickets cannot move directly from CLOSED to PENDING."
distractors: "Closed tickets must reopen to OPEN before other workflow transitions."
No error: CLOSED to PENDING is allowed, so the change goes through
"This role cannot change ticket workflow status." from the policy
items.explanation: assertValidStatusTransition runs first; CLOSED allows only OPEN, so it throws the table's conflict. The closed-ticket check on the next lines is never reached.

items.prompt: POST /escalate on a PENDING ticket. What is missing from the result?
items.answer: A transition check and the status-history row for the change
distractors: Nothing, as escalation runs through changeTicketStatus like other moves
The audit log row, since escalations are never audited in this service
The status change itself, which stays PENDING until the next write
items.explanation: escalateTicket writes status ESCALATED directly (F7): the timeline shows an escalation but no status change, and SLA tracking is not re-evaluated, so a PENDING ticket stays paused until the next write.

items.front: The ticket state machine: shape and the paths that bypass it
items.back: An adjacency map with 25 allowed edges between 7 states, plus a free pass for self-transitions. Only changeTicketStatus consults it; addPublicReply and escalateTicket write status directly.

items.front: Two ways the support-hub unit tests overstate their coverage
items.back: The SLA test asserts only the PAUSED label, not resume or accumulation. The schema test passes five invalid fields at once and asserts success === false, so any one rule would make it pass and it cannot say which rule rejected the payload.

Nothing calls it. It also runs each ticket's writes outside a transaction, loads every active ticket with no paging, sets isEscalated even when it skips the escalation record, and never sets status ESCALATED. Dashboard 'breached' counts therefore show whatever was persisted at the last write.

items.front: How are SLA deadlines computed, and what is missing?
items.back: createdAt + N wall-clock minutes. No business hours, holidays or time zones: a 24-hour target set Friday 17:00 UTC falls due Saturday 17:00 UTC; paused time is never credited.
